title: Natural cycle-to-homology comparison for section complexes before deriving
statement: Let f:X\to Y be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] and q\in\mathbf N. On the category of nonnegative cochain complexes C of O_X-modules [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules; def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], there is a natural homomorphism tau_C:H^q(Gamma(X,C))\to Gamma(Y,H^q(f_*C)), using direct image [def-pc-ringed-spaces-derived-direct-image] and sections [def-sc-ringed-space-module-cohomology]. For every cycle s of Gamma(X,C), there is a section z of Z^q(f_*C) whose image in Gamma(Y,f_*C^q) is the section s transported along f^{-1}(Y)=X, and tau_C applied to the homology class of s is Gamma(Y,pi)(z), where pi:Z^q(f_*C)\to H^q(f_*C) is the canonical homology quotient. The two equations are those in the Lean signature. Here H^q of a complex is its kernel modulo the image of the incoming differential [def-sp-abelian], and no resolution or injectivity hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 01F4, lemma-apply-Leray, proof: direct-proof exercise, the comparison on complexes before choosing resolutions; universal-property details expanded by K1

proof.text: For a nonnegative cochain complex C of O_X-modules, direct image on the whole target evaluates C on f^{-1}(Y)=X. The restriction along Opens.map_top is a natural isomorphism of the underlying abelian-group section complexes. Global sections is evaluation and preserves kernels: the universal kernel property, evaluated on Y, identifies cycles of the section complex with sections of the cycle sheaf of f_* C. Thus every cycle s has a unique section z whose cycle inclusion is the transported section s.

Compose this identification with sections of the quotient Z^q(f_* C) to H^q(f_* C). An incoming differential lands in B^q(f_* C) and hence has zero image in this quotient. The resulting additive map on global cycles therefore annihilates the global boundaries. By the cokernel universal property defining homology it factors uniquely to a homomorphism H^q(Gamma(X,C)) to Gamma(Y,H^q(f_* C)). In degree zero the incoming differential is zero, so the same argument applies. This factorization gives the stated homology equation.

For a cochain map C to Cprime, the two candidate composites on homology agree after precomposition with the cycles-to-homology quotient: the kernel lift, cycle inclusion, and homology quotient all commute with cochain maps. That quotient is epic in modules, so the two maps agree. Thus the homomorphisms of the preceding step form the natural transformation tau. The two equations of the statement are precisely the kernel-lift and cokernel-factorization equations. No injectivity, acyclicity, or resolution choice is used.

theorem leray_complex_cocycle_comparison {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) (q : ℕ) :
    ∃ τ :
      ((RingedSpace.globalSectionsFunctor X.toRingedSpace).mapHomologicalComplex
        (ComplexShape.up ℕ) ⋙ HomologicalComplex.homologyFunctor _ _ q ⋙
          forget₂ _ AddCommGrpCat) ⟶
      ((RingedSpace.moduleDirectImage f.toLRSHom.toShHom).mapHomologicalComplex
        (ComplexShape.up ℕ) ⋙ HomologicalComplex.homologyFunctor _ _ q ⋙
          RingedSpace.globalSectionsFunctor Y.toRingedSpace ⋙ forget₂ _ AddCommGrpCat),
      ∀ (C : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace)) ℕ)
        (s : (((RingedSpace.globalSectionsFunctor X.toRingedSpace).mapHomologicalComplex
          (ComplexShape.up ℕ)).obj C).cycles q),
        ∃ z : (RingedSpace.globalSectionsFunctor Y.toRingedSpace).obj
          ((((RingedSpace.moduleDirectImage f.toLRSHom.toShHom).mapHomologicalComplex
            (ComplexShape.up ℕ)).obj C).cycles q),
          (C.X q).val.presheaf.map
            (eqToHom (congrArg op (Opens.map_top f.base).symm))
            ((((RingedSpace.globalSectionsFunctor X.toRingedSpace).mapHomologicalComplex
              (ComplexShape.up ℕ)).obj C).iCycles q s) =
            (RingedSpace.globalSectionsFunctor Y.toRingedSpace).map
              ((((RingedSpace.moduleDirectImage f.toLRSHom.toShHom).mapHomologicalComplex
                (ComplexShape.up ℕ)).obj C).iCycles q) z ∧
          (τ.app C)
            ((((RingedSpace.globalSectionsFunctor X.toRingedSpace).mapHomologicalComplex
              (ComplexShape.up ℕ)).obj C).homologyπ q s) =
            (RingedSpace.globalSectionsFunctor Y.toRingedSpace).map
              ((((RingedSpace.moduleDirectImage f.toLRSHom.toShHom).mapHomologicalComplex
                (ComplexShape.up ℕ)).obj C).homologyπ q) z
